1. For chained nodes (dialer-proxy), an inner node showing “underlying 0” is normal: the physical socket is counted on the first hop.

2. QUIC-based nodes (hysteria, tuic) use a single UDP socket for the whole session. The underlying count cannot tell you whether multiplexing is working.

3. After you close a website, the count does not drop to zero immediately. Idle multiplexed connections are kept open for a while.

4. “Underlying” counts every socket the core opens for the node, including node health checks, latency tests, DNS queries through the node, and temporary connections created when this app tests other IPs. These are not in the connections list, so they are not upper connections. While idle, you may therefore see “underlying 3 / upper connections 0”.

5. A socket discarded without being closed normally is removed from the count only after Go garbage collection runs its cleanup finalizer, so the count can stay temporarily high.

6. With smux statistic: true, the carrier connection itself is also counted as an upper connection.

7. A country flag is shown only when the app already knows the IP’s country/region (from a test or probe). No extra lookup is made just to show a flag.
Underlying = TCP sockets the core actually keeps open to the node. Upper connections = connections carried by the node; with multiplexing, underlying should be far fewer.

Tap “ECH check” to make a real network connection and check the configured ech-opts. For the ECH check, enter a domain known to be blocked and hosted by the node server or a CDN in front of it. DNS check accepts any domain. Direct latency uses this domain as SNI and Host; to read the ingress data centre, the domain must be on Cloudflare. Certificates are not verified; only handshake success is checked. DNS check asks each configured DNS server about the same domain (only dns: and hosts: are read).
